Energy per pound of weight lost
The classic rule of thumb, which equals about 7,700 kcal per kg and varies with body fat.
3,500 kcal per lb
diet-term-energy-deficit
Energy deficit
Eating less energy than you use. It is the one requirement for losing body fat. A daily deficit of 500 kcal is about 3,500 kcal a week.
diet-table-deficit-rate
Deficit size versus expected weekly loss
Approximate weekly loss for a daily deficit at 7,700 kcal per kg (3,500 per lb), for an 80 kg (176 lb) person. Leaner people tend to lose more weight than this.
diet-protein-in-deficit
Eat more protein when you diet: about 2.3 to 3.1 g per kg of lean mass
Lean lifters in a deficit kept more muscle with higher protein, around 2.3 to 3.1 g per kg of fat-free mass.
diet-lift-in-deficit
Keep lifting while dieting, because training tells the body to keep muscle
Resistance training reduced the lean mass lost in a diet, and strength was largely kept in deficit trials.
diet-sleep-in-deficit
Short sleep shifts diet loss toward muscle and away from fat
In ten adults, five and a half hours of sleep cut the fat share of weight lost by 55 percent.
diet-mistake-low-protein-no-lifting
Cutting protein and stopping lifting while dieting
The two habits that protect muscle in a deficit are protein and heavy training, and dropping both costs lean mass.
diet-num-protein-deficit
Protein in a deficit
ISSN and review ranges for lean lifters dieting; raise it as the deficit and leanness grow.
2.3-3.1 g per kg lean mass
diet-hunger-protein-food
Protein and unprocessed food help control hunger, at least in the short run
Protein reduced hunger in meal studies, and a ward trial found unprocessed meals led to about 500 kcal less intake.
diet-appetite-rises
Appetite rises as you lose weight, so hunger is part of the process
In one 52-week trial, appetite rose enough to add about 100 kcal a day per kg of weight lost.
diet-num-appetite
Appetite rise per kg of weight lost
In one trial, eating drifted above baseline by about this much for each kilogram lost.
100 kcal per day per kg
diet-energy-density
Water-rich fruit and vegetables lower hunger for the same calories
In one year-long trial, women who ate more water-rich foods lost more weight and reported less hunger.
diet-metabolic-adaptation
Metabolic slowdown with dieting is real but smaller than most people fear
Adaptation is real but small, tens to low hundreds of kcal a day in most studies, so check your log first.
diet-scale-noise
Day-to-day weight changes are mostly water, so read the trend
Two-week changes of 1 to 3 kg were largely fat-free mass and water, not fat, in free-living adults.
diet-stall-not-failure
A two-week stall is not proof your diet stopped working
Check logging and weekend intake before cutting calories, since stalls are usually noise or under-logging.
diet-mistake-react-to-stall
Cutting calories after a short stall
Short stalls are mostly water and weekend noise, and cutting on them stacks deficit on top of a working plan.
diet-num-short-term-density
Energy per kg for short-term changes
Two-week changes of 1 to 3 kg were mostly fat-free mass and water, so they carry less energy than fat.
2,380 kcal per kg
diet-term-adaptive-thermogenesis
Adaptive thermogenesis (metabolic adaptation)
A fall in energy use beyond what the loss of body mass explains, seen during and after weight loss. Studies find it ranges from small to modest.
diet-table-scale-moves
What moves scale weight day to day
Short-term causes of scale changes that are not fat gain or loss.
diet-self-weighing
Weighing yourself regularly goes with more loss inside a programme
Programmes that included self-weighing beat minimal care by 3.4 kg, and daily weighing did no better than weekly.
diet-term-set-point
Set point and settling point

Two models of body weight: a defended set point, or a settling point where weight drifts with food and activity. A review finds both incomplete. McDonald's view is that the body resists loss far more than gain.
diet-diet-breaks
Diet breaks and refeeds give mixed fat-loss results and may ease hunger
Planned weeks at maintenance did not improve fat loss in lifters, and they lowered hunger.
diet-diet-type
The best diet is the one you can keep to, since types differ little
Low-carb and low-fat diets lost about the same weight, so pick the one you can keep.
diet-intermittent-fasting
Intermittent fasting works by eating less, with no clear extra effect
Time-restricted eating did not beat plain calorie control in long trials, though one pooled analysis disagrees.
diet-meal-frequency-timing
Meal frequency and late eating matter little for fat loss at equal calories
Differences between meal patterns are small at equal calories; fewer meals showed about 1 kg more loss in one analysis.
diet-term-diet-break
Diet break and refeed
A diet break is a planned stretch, often one to two weeks, at maintenance calories. A refeed is shorter, usually one or two days of higher carbohydrate.
diet-term-time-restricted-eating
Time-restricted eating
Eating all meals within a set daily window, such as eight hours, and fasting for the rest. It is one form of intermittent fasting.
diet-adherence-beats-diet-type
Weight lost tracked sticking to the diet, not which diet it was
In one year-long trial, weight lost followed how closely people kept to their diet, with no link to the diet they chose.
diet-cardio-and-steps
Exercise adds to fat loss, and daily movement drops on diets if you let it
Exercise adds 1.5 to 3.5 kg of loss in reviews, and people on diets may move less outside the gym.
diet-term-neat
NEAT (non-exercise activity)
Non-exercise activity thermogenesis: energy spent on walking, standing, fidgeting and chores. It can fall during a diet without you noticing.
diet-very-lean-costs
Getting very lean costs hormones, mood and training quality, so go carefully
Long spells under about 25 kcal per kg of lean mass led to muscle loss and hormone and mood problems in men. In women, 30 marks rising risk, not a cut-off.
diet-regain-and-maintenance
Weight regain is common, and maintenance is possible with sustained habits
Most people regain some weight. A minority keep most of it off, and they report steady activity and regular weighing.
diet-mistake-no-end-plan
Dieting with no end date and no plan for after
Regain follows the diet for most people, and a plan for the exit matters as much as the deficit.
diet-surplus-size
A small surplus adds muscle, and a large surplus mostly adds fat
A surplus of about 10 to 20 percent over maintenance is a common starting range for lifters, and nobody has proven the best size.
diet-recomposition
Recomposition works best for beginners, returners and people carrying more fat
Gaining muscle while losing fat is realistic with high protein and hard training, and likely harder for lean, advanced lifters.
diet-mistake-dirty-bulk
Treating a gaining phase as a licence to eat anything
A large surplus mainly added fat in a trial, and extra fat has to be dieted off later.
diet-num-surplus
Surplus for a gaining phase
Suggested range for novice and intermediate lifters in a physique-sport review; advanced lifters go lower.
10-20 % above maintenance
diet-num-gain-rate
Rate of gain, novice to intermediate
At 80 kg (176 lb) that is 0.2 to 0.4 kg (0.4 to 0.9 lb) a week.
0.25-0.5 % body weight per week
diet-term-recomposition
Recomposition
Gaining muscle and losing fat over the same period. Body weight may hold steady or fall while the body changes shape.
diet-table-gain-rate
Rate of gain by training age
Suggested pace of weight gain in a gaining phase; the research is thin and the rates are conservative.
diet-deficit-percent-of-maintenance
Size the deficit as a share of maintenance, not a fixed calorie number
A percentage cut scales with the person: 20 percent is 360 kcal a day at 1,800 kcal maintenance and 600 kcal at 3,000.
diet-table-deficit-by-size
The same percentage deficit at two maintenance levels
Daily deficit and a first-pass weekly loss at 7,700 kcal per kg (3,500 per lb). On far larger deficits, supervised dieters lost about a quarter less than the rule predicts in about 65 days.
diet-mistake-tiny-deficit-loose-logging
Running a 10 percent deficit while logging food loosely
A deficit of 200 to 300 kcal a day is within reach of label and logging error, so it can vanish without you noticing.
diet-fast-loss-regain
Losing weight quickly did not mean regaining it faster in a long trial
Of 200 adults with obesity, those who reached the target had regained about 71 percent by week 144, whether the loss was rapid or gradual.
diet-fixed-intake-plateau
A fixed calorie cut slows to a plateau because the gap closes as you shrink
On a fixed cut a shrinking body burns less, so loss slows and stops. Supervised dieters fell about a quarter short of the 3,500 rule in about 65 days.
diet-num-intake-change-rule
Eventual weight change per lasting change in daily intake
About 10 kcal a day per lb. A rule of thumb from one validated model: in an average overweight adult, half arrives within a year and 95 percent within about three.
100 kJ a day per kg of change
diet-mistake-first-week-drop
Reading a big first-week drop on low carb as fast fat loss
An early drop on low carb is mostly stored glycogen and the water held with it, and fat loss did not speed up on a ketogenic diet in a ward study.
diet-setup-order
Set up a fat-loss diet in order: calories, protein, fat, then carbohydrate
Fix the calorie target first, then protein, then a moderate fat intake, and let carbohydrate fill whatever is left.
diet-athlete-fuel-training
Athletes in a deficit should keep food around hard sessions and cut elsewhere
When an athlete trims carbohydrate to diet, the cut should come from meals away from hard training, not from the meals that fuel it.
diet-athlete-weight-timing
Athletes should diet in a low-intensity training block, not close to competition
Plan fat loss for the off-season or a general preparation block, and aim for a weight you can hold for most of the year.
diet-num-early-loss-energy
Energy in each kg lost at week four of a diet
Rose to about 6,000 by week six in 23 overweight adults. Still below the rule's 7,700, so each kg lost early needs a smaller deficit than the rule assumes.
about 4,900 kcal per kg lost
diet-term-rigid-flexible
Rigid and flexible restraint
Two styles of holding back on food. Rigid control runs on fixed rules and forbidden foods, all or nothing. Flexible control allows any food in limited amounts and evens out over days.
diet-flexible-control
Flexible control of eating goes with lower weight and fewer binges than rigid rules
In large surveys, people who allowed limited amounts of any food weighed less and binged less than people who ran on strict food rules.
diet-mistake-lapse-spiral
Treating one off-plan snack as a ruined diet
A 200 kcal treat is under a tenth of a 3,500 kcal weekly deficit. Giving up on the day because of it is what costs you.
diet-mistake-cutting-fruit
Dropping whole fruit from a fat-loss diet
In a six-week trial in adults with obesity, a calorie-restricted diet with fruit lost more weight than one that kept fructose very low.
diet-adjust-in-steps
When the trend says change, move calories about 10 percent and wait again
Adjust intake or activity in steps of about a tenth, then reassess after two to three weeks, or four if water swings hide the trend.
diet-holiday-gain
Holiday weight gain is small on average, but it tends to stay
In 195 adults, weight rose about 0.4 kg over the winter holidays, far below the 2.3 kg (5 lb) often claimed, and the gain was not lost in the months after.
diet-breakfast
Skipping breakfast did not hurt weight control in short trials
In a meta-analysis of short trials, people assigned to breakfast ate about 260 kcal a day more and weighed slightly more than people assigned to skip it.
diet-mistake-dropping-dairy
Cutting out dairy for a diet or contest prep
Dairy did not change weight overall in a meta-analysis, but in calorie-restricted trials it gave slightly more weight and fat loss.
diet-mistake-protein-as-percent
Setting protein as a percentage of calories during a diet
A fixed share of calories gives less protein as calories fall, just when lean lifters in a deficit likely need more. Set protein in grams per kg instead.
diet-term-glycaemic-index
Glycaemic index (GI)

How far a food's carbohydrate raises blood glucose against the same amount from glucose or white bread. Fat, protein and fibre in a meal lower it, and in studies GI did not change how much fat people burned.
diet-term-tkd-ckd
Targeted and cyclical ketogenic diets

Ketogenic diets adapted for hard training. A targeted version adds a small dose of carbohydrate around sessions; a cyclical one alternates several low-carbohydrate days with one or two days of high carbohydrate.
diet-prescribed-breaks
Planned time off the diet did not cut total weight loss in a trial
In 142 adults in a behavioural weight-loss programme, scheduled breaks from dieting left total loss at 5 and 11 months unchanged.
diet-break-carb-floor
McDonald keeps carbohydrate at 120 to 150 g a day or more on a diet break
McDonald sets a carbohydrate floor of about 120 to 150 g a day for a diet break, on the view that thyroid hormone needs it.
diet-break-spacing
McDonald spaces diet breaks by body fat, so leaner dieters take them sooner
In McDonald's practice, lean dieters take a break every 4 to 6 weeks, while people carrying more fat go 12 to 16 weeks between breaks.
diet-post-diet-protein
Higher protein after a diet halved weight regain in one trial
In 148 overweight to moderately obese adults after a diet, about 48 g a day of extra protein halved regain over 3 months, and the regain was fat-free mass.
diet-post-contest-regain
After a physique contest, regain came first as water and later mostly as fat
In 15 natural physique athletes, weight and body water rose soon after competing, and fat mass climbed about 2 kg by 4 to 6 weeks later.
diet-low-days-on-rest-days
McDonald puts the low days of an intermittent restriction plan on rest days
Two very low days a week lost as much as a daily cut in overweight women. McDonald's view is that the low days must miss hard training.
diet-gut-energy-harvest
Gut bacteria went with a difference of about 150 kcal in energy absorbed
In 21 inpatients, shifts in gut bacteria went with changes in the calories lost in stool, about 150 kcal in lean people.
diet-term-nutrient-balance
Nutrient balance (protein, carbohydrate and fat balance)

Intake minus oxidation for one nutrient. In 54 adults in a chamber, the body matched carbohydrate and protein burning to intake, so day-to-day surpluses and gaps landed almost entirely on fat balance.
diet-alcohol-fat-burning
Alcohol cut the fat burned by about a third on the day it was drunk
In 8 men in a chamber, alcohol at a quarter of daily energy cut fat burning by about a third that day, while carbohydrate and protein burning held.
diet-protein-not-low-carb
The higher protein in low-carb diets, not the low carb, drove loss in one trial
In 132 adults with obesity, high-protein diets lost more over a year than normal-protein ones, while low-carb against normal-carb made no difference.
diet-checklist-any-diet
What any fat-loss diet needs before its details matter
McDonald's list. Check a plan against it before worrying about meal timing or macro ratios. The first group is essential; the second decides whether you can keep it up.
diet-same-surplus-different-gain
The same surplus added 4 to 13 kg in different men, and twins responded alike
Twelve pairs of young identical twin men overfed by 1,000 kcal a day gained 4.3 to 13.3 kg, with brothers more alike than unrelated men.
diet-mistake-low-fat-halo
Eating more of a food because it is labelled low-fat or diet-approved
Women told a yogurt was low-fat ate more at the next meal than after a yogurt of similar calories labelled high-fat.
diet-mistake-goal-a-third
Setting a goal of losing a third of your body weight in one go
Sixty women with obesity aimed to lose 32 percent of their weight. After 48 weeks and a 16 kg loss, nearly half had not reached even the result they called disappointing.
diet-term-false-hope
False hope syndrome

Polivy and Herman's name for a cycle of repeated self-change attempts driven by unrealistic hopes about how fast, how far and how easily change will come, and what it will bring. Failure is followed by a fresh attempt.
diet-num-post-obese-rmr
Resting metabolic rate in formerly obese adults
Two pooled 1999 analyses, adjusted for body composition: 2.9 percent lower (not significant) and 5.1 percent. Later work is mixed; see the metabolic adaptation entry.
3-5 percent below never-obese
diet-keto-no-edge
A ketogenic diet lost no more fat than a moderate-carb diet in a controlled trial
In 20 sedentary adults with obesity on controlled food for 6 weeks, ketogenic and moderate-carb diets did not differ significantly in weight or fat lost.
diet-table-protein-carb-trial
Protein against carbohydrate: loss at 12 months in four diets
Mean loss in 132 adults with obesity: 3 months at a third of energy needs (a supervised-only intake), then 9 at two thirds. Low carb did not beat normal carb (see the protein entry).
diet-term-negative-calorie
Negative calorie illusion (dieter's paradox)
The mistaken belief that adding a healthy food to an unhealthy meal lowers its calories. In Chernev's studies the error was larger in people most concerned with their weight.
diet-maintenance-loading
In a diet, McDonald cuts heavy volume from the start and keeps the load
McDonald's practice is to drop heavy volume by up to two thirds when a diet begins, hold the usual loads, and fill any time saved with cardio or light work.
diet-antidepressants-weight
Antidepressants differ in their effect on weight, so raise changes with the prescriber
A meta-analysis of 116 studies linked some antidepressants to weight gain and others to little change or slight loss, with wide individual variation.
diet-heal-before-dieting
After surgery or injury, McDonald's advice is to heal first and diet later
In McDonald's view, healing raises energy needs and a deficit may slow repair, so a little fat gained while recovering is the smaller problem.
comp-term-body-composition
Body composition
What your body weight is made of. The simplest model has two parts. One is fat. The other, fat-free mass, is everything else: muscle, bone, organs, blood, water and stored carbohydrate.
comp-term-fat-free-mass
Fat-free mass or lean body mass (FFM, LBM)
All of the body that is not fat. In everyday use the two terms mean the same thing. Muscle is only part of it, and its water and glycogen content can shift by a kilo or more within days.
comp-fat-loss-moves-percentage-more
Losing fat lowers body fat percentage far more than gaining the same weight of muscle
A kilo of fat lost moves your body fat percentage about three times as far as a kilo of muscle gained, and it happens much sooner.
comp-table-arithmetic
Body composition arithmetic
The five sums used in this area, worked for a person of 80 kg (176 lb), 1.80 m (5 ft 11 in) and 25 percent body fat.
comp-mistake-all-loss-is-fat
Planning a target weight as if every kilo lost will be fat
The target-weight sum assumes lean mass stays put. Some water, glycogen and lean tissue always go too, so you reach the number less lean than planned.
comp-methods-estimate
Every body fat method estimates, and none measures fat directly
Scans, calipers and scales each measure something else (X-ray absorption, skin thickness, electrical resistance, density) and convert it with assumptions that may not fit you.
comp-consistency-over-accuracy
For tracking change, a consistent method beats an accurate one
A tool that is wrong by the same amount every time still shows whether you gained or lost, and by roughly how much.
comp-table-methods
Body fat methods: what each one really measures
What each common method senses, where its error comes from and what it is good for.
comp-num-field-error
Individual error of field methods in bodybuilders
Error of DXA, skinfolds, bioimpedance and BMI equations for single individuals against a four-compartment model in 27 male bodybuilders.
5.5-8 body fat points
comp-dxa-reads-higher
DXA reads several points higher than skinfold equations
Three standard skinfold equations came out 3.1 to 3.3 points below DXA in 160 men and 3.2 to 5.6 points below in 150 women.
comp-num-dxa-offset
How far skinfold equations read below DXA
Three recommended skinfold equations against same-day DXA: 3.1 to 3.3 points low in 160 men, 3.2 to 5.6 low in 150 women.
3-6 body fat points
comp-mistake-mixing-methods
Comparing a body fat number from one method with a number from another
A 14 percent DXA scan and a 10 percent caliper reading can describe the same body, so switching methods mid-diet invents or hides progress.
comp-skinfold-sum
With calipers, track the sum of folds in millimetres
The millimetre total from the same sites is the dependable part of a caliper test. The percentage comes from an equation that may not suit you.
comp-bia-hydration
Bioimpedance scales read body water, so hydration changes the answer
A body fat scale sends a small current through you, estimates water from the resistance and predicts fat from that. A change in water looks like a change in fat.
comp-water-reads-as-lean
A fast change in lean mass is water and glycogen, not muscle
Loading or emptying muscle glycogen moved DXA lean mass by 2 to 3 percent within days in trained cyclists, with no real change in muscle.
comp-strength-as-check
Gym strength is a practical check on muscle during a diet
If body weight is falling and your main lifts are holding, what you are losing is unlikely to be muscle.
comp-checklist-tracking
A tracking routine that works with imperfect tools
Fixed conditions and a small set of repeated measures tell you more than any single precise test.
comp-how-often-to-measure
How often to measure depends on how much fat you carry
When fat stores are large, weekly change is too small for any tool to see, so judge monthly. Very lean dieters change fast enough to check weekly.
comp-mistake-inconsistent-conditions
Comparing readings taken under different conditions
A Friday evening reading after meals and a Monday morning reading on an empty stomach differ for reasons unrelated to fat.
comp-cycle-phase
With a menstrual cycle, compare the same week month to month
Fluid retention rises and falls across the cycle, so week-to-week comparisons can show a false gain or hide a real loss.
comp-lower-limit-men
Healthy men bottom out at about 4 to 6 percent body fat
Below roughly 4 to 6 percent by DXA, further weight loss in men came mostly from fat-free mass, not fat.
comp-num-lower-limit-men
Lower limit of body fat in healthy men
In 55 soldiers losing weight over 8 weeks, loss beyond this level came mostly from fat-free mass. It equals about 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) of fat.
4-6 % body fat (DXA)
comp-term-essential-fat
Essential fat
The fat the body cannot give up and stay healthy, held in nerves, bone marrow, organs and cell membranes. In healthy men the measured floor is about 4 to 6 percent of body weight. Women's is higher.
comp-table-athlete-body-fat
Measured body fat in athletes by sport (DXA)
Mean whole-body fat by DXA in 481 athletes scanned at one laboratory in Portugal. DXA reads higher than calipers, so do not set these beside skinfold figures.
comp-num-sex-gap
Gap in body fat between women and men athletes
By DXA, 143 women athletes averaged 23.5 percent and 339 men 13.9 percent across the sports sampled.
about 10 body fat points
comp-sport-sets-body-fat
Each sport has a body fat level that suits it, and leaner is not always faster or stronger
Sports where you carry your body against gravity run leanest. Contact, throwing and water sports sit higher, and going below a sport's usual range tends to cost performance.
comp-abs-and-legs
Men and women lean out in a different order
Men usually see lean legs well before a lean waist. Women usually see their midsection first, with hips and thighs last.
comp-term-android-gynoid
Android and gynoid fat patterns

Android means fat carried on the trunk and abdomen, the usual male pattern. Gynoid means fat on hips and thighs, more common in women before menopause. Upper-body fat is linked to more heart disease and type 2 diabetes.
comp-term-adipose
Adipose tissue and adipocytes
Adipose tissue is body fat. Its cells, adipocytes, store energy as triglyceride and release hormones such as leptin, so fat acts as a gland as well as a fuel store.
comp-term-fat-depots
Subcutaneous, visceral and ectopic fat

Subcutaneous fat lies under the skin and can be pinched. Visceral fat surrounds the abdominal organs. Ectopic fat is fat stored inside organs such as the liver. Visceral and ectopic fat carry the most cardiometabolic risk.
comp-fat-cell-number
Dieting shrinks fat cells and does not remove them
Adult fat cell number stayed constant in lean and obese people, even after marked weight loss, while overfeeding added cells in the lower body within 8 weeks.
comp-fat-compact-store
Fat holds far more energy than glycogen in far less weight
Glycogen stores top out near 15 g per kg of body weight and carry three to four times their weight in water. Body fat stores about 7,700 kcal per kg.
comp-num-glycogen-capacity
Glycogen storage capacity
Measured in three men during a week of massive carbohydrate overfeeding. Each gram is stored with three to four grams of water.
about 15 g per kg body weight
comp-surplus-routes
Any surplus adds body fat, by a different route for each nutrient
Extra dietary fat is stored almost directly. Extra carbohydrate is mostly burned, which spares the fat you ate, and that fat is stored.
comp-mistake-carbs-cannot-fatten
Assuming extra carbohydrate or protein cannot become body fat
Carbohydrate is rarely converted to fat, but a carbohydrate surplus still makes you fatter by letting dietary fat go into storage.
comp-term-dnl
De novo lipogenesis (DNL)
The making of new fat from carbohydrate. In people it is a minor route on ordinary diets and becomes large only when glycogen stores are full during heavy, sustained carbohydrate overfeeding.
comp-stubborn-depots
Hip, thigh and lower abdominal fat is released more slowly than other fat
Fat depots differ in how readily they give up fat. Abdominal and visceral stores turn over fast, and lower-body stores turn over slowly.
comp-term-adrenoceptors
Alpha-2 and beta adrenoceptors

Receptors on fat cells for adrenaline and noradrenaline. Beta receptors switch fat release on and alpha-2 receptors switch it off. A depot with relatively more alpha-2 receptors lets go of fat more slowly.
comp-mistake-judging-one-spot
Judging a diet by the one area that changes last
Fat usually leaves faster-releasing areas first, so the lower abdomen, hips or thighs can look unchanged for weeks while total fat is falling.
comp-stepwise-loss
Scale loss often arrives in steps, with water hiding fat loss in between
Some dieters see nothing for one to three weeks and then drop a kilo (2 lb) or more almost overnight. The fat was going all along.
comp-term-whoosh
Whoosh

Informal name for a sudden drop in scale weight, often a kilo or more overnight, after days or weeks with no change on a diet. It is thought to be retained water leaving. The mechanism has not been shown in studies.
comp-term-partitioning
Calorie partitioning
Where energy goes or comes from when intake changes: how much of a surplus builds muscle and how much is stored as fat, and how much of a deficit is met from fat and how much from lean tissue.
comp-term-p-ratio
P-ratio
The share of a change in body energy that comes from protein, which stands for lean tissue. A low P-ratio during a diet means the loss was mostly fat. A high one means much of it was lean.
comp-forbes-body-fat-sets-share
How much fat you carry sets how much of a weight change is lean tissue
Fatter people lose mostly fat when they diet and gain mostly fat when overfed. Thinner people lose and gain a larger share of lean tissue.
comp-table-forbes
Lean share of a weight change, by starting body fat
Findings from Forbes's review of feeding studies, with the classic dieting rule for comparison. The people studied were not lifting.
comp-num-quarter-rule
Lean share of weight lost under the classic rule
The 'quarter fat-free mass rule' for dieting with obesity. A 2014 review found the share varies with time, age, activity and exercise.
about 25 % of weight lost
comp-mistake-diet-lean-to-bulk
Getting extremely lean first so the next bulk will 'partition better'
Naturally thin people gain a large share of lean tissue when overfed. People who have dieted down do not behave like them, and the body restores fat first.
comp-gaining-range
McDonald's working body fat range for a gaining phase
His judgment is that men gain best starting from about 10 to 12 percent body fat in caliper terms and should diet back at about 15, with women roughly ten points higher.
comp-why-lean-lose-lean
Lean tissue loss speeds up as you get leaner
With less fat to draw on, more of each kilo lost comes from lean tissue, and the hormonal response to dieting grows stronger.
comp-what-controls-partitioning
Most of partitioning is outside your control, and a few levers are not
Hormones, genetics and current body fat decide most of where calories go. Training, protein and the size of the surplus or deficit shift the rest.
comp-term-leptin
Leptin
A hormone made mainly by fat cells. Blood levels rise with body fat and fall quickly when you eat less, so it tells the brain both how much energy is stored and whether food is coming in.
comp-defence-is-lopsided
The body resists fat loss much harder than it resists fat gain
Energy expenditure falls and hunger rises when weight is lost. The opposing response to overeating is weak in most people.
comp-leptin-tracks-fat
People with more body fat have more leptin, not less
Leptin rises almost in step with body fat percentage, so obesity is a state of high leptin that the brain responds to poorly.
comp-num-leptin-sex
Leptin in women compared with men at equal fat mass
15.2 against 6.9 ng per ml in 63 women and 333 men whose average fat mass was the same, about 20.5 kg (45 lb).
about 2x serum leptin
comp-leptin-falls-fast
Leptin responds to food intake within days, and to carbohydrate more than fat
Three days of carbohydrate overfeeding raised leptin by 28 percent in lean women. The same excess energy as fat did not change it.
comp-leptin-restores
Putting leptin back reverses much of the weight-reduced state
In people held at 10 percent below their usual weight, restoring leptin to its old level returned energy expenditure and thyroid hormones to pre-loss values.
comp-band-then-biology
Small weight changes follow habits, and large losses meet biological resistance
McDonald's synthesis: within a band around your current weight, food environment and activity decide where you sit. Push well below it and the body pushes back.
comp-levine-variation
The same surplus made some people store ten times the fat of others
Sixteen adults ate 1,000 kcal a day above maintenance for 8 weeks. Fat storage differed ten-fold between them, and the difference tracked non-exercise activity.
comp-num-levine-neat
Share of the extra energy burned in overfeeding that came from NEAT
In 16 adults overfed by 1,000 kcal a day for 8 weeks. The change in NEAT predicted resistance to fat gain (r = 0.77).
about 2/3 of the rise in expenditure
comp-term-thrifty-spendthrift
Thrifty and spendthrift metabolism

Labels for how energy expenditure responds to intake. In 14 men, 24-hour expenditure rose about 9 percent with two days of double feeding and fell about 9 percent with fasting, and the two responses were correlated between individuals.
comp-predicted-vs-actual-loss
Diets produce less than half the predicted loss, mostly through adherence
A review of low-calorie diet studies found actual weight loss under half of what the prescribed deficit predicts, with food absorption unchanged.
comp-term-ffmi
Fat-free mass index (FFMI)
Fat-free mass (kg) over the square of height (m). It is the lean-mass version of BMI and lets you compare muscularity between people of different heights.
comp-kouri-ceiling
In the original study, drug-free athletes topped out at an FFMI of 25
Among 157 male athletes, the 74 who had never used steroids reached a height-normalized FFMI of 25.0 and no higher. Many users exceeded it.
comp-num-ffmi-25
FFMI where drug-free athletes topped out
Upper edge for 74 non-users in a 1995 study of 157 male athletes. Many steroid users exceeded it and some passed 30.
25 kg/m2, height-normalized
comp-ffmi-not-a-drug-test
Treat an FFMI of 25 as a rare ceiling, not as a drug test
Lyle McDonald's position is that a few genetically unusual lifters pass 25 without drugs, and that for nearly everyone else it marks the practical limit.
comp-mistake-ffmi-high-fat
Reading a high FFMI at high body fat as muscle
Fat-free mass rises as people get fatter, because extra fat brings water, connective tissue and other non-muscle lean tissue with it. FFMI rises too, without more muscle.
comp-baseline-shapes-ffmi
Where you start shapes where you finish
People begin training with very different amounts of lean mass, so the same FFMI can mean a large gain for one lifter and almost none for another.
comp-career-muscle-gain
Drug-free muscle gain is front-loaded: most arrives in the first two or three years
McDonald's model predicts that yearly muscle gain roughly halves from one well-trained year to the next, giving men a career total near 18 to 23 kg (40 to 50 lb).
comp-num-career-gain
Career muscle gain predicted for men by McDonald's model
His estimate of total drug-free muscle gained over four or more years of proper training. Women about half. A coaching model, not a study result.
comp-mistake-beginner-rates-forever
Expecting beginner rates of muscle gain after years of training
An experienced lifter who eats for the gains of a first-year trainee adds fat at the rate the surplus allows and muscle at the rate biology allows.
comp-table-ffmi-reference
FFMI reference points from published samples
Where measured groups fall on the fat-free mass index. Methods differ, so treat the rows as rough landmarks.
comp-term-bmr-rmr
BMR and RMR

Basal metabolic rate is the lowest energy use the body can run on, measured under strict conditions. Resting metabolic rate is measured awake, fasted and lying quietly, and reads a little higher. Most labs and equations give RMR.
comp-table-energy-components
The four parts of daily energy expenditure
McDonald's four-part breakdown of energy out, with how far each part moves between people and over time.
comp-organs-drive-rmr
A few organs, not muscle, do most of the resting calorie burn
At rest the liver, brain, heart and kidneys use 200 to 440 kcal per kg a day. Muscle uses about 13 and fat tissue about 4.5.
comp-table-tissue-energy
Resting energy use by tissue
Per-kilo resting energy use of the main tissues, from values proposed by Elia and evaluated in 131 adults.
comp-num-muscle-rmr
Resting energy use of muscle
About 6 kcal per lb. Fat tissue uses about 4.5 kcal per kg (2 per lb), while the liver and brain use 200 or more.
13 kcal per kg per day
comp-mistake-muscle-metabolism
Building muscle to 'speed up your metabolism'
Five kilos (11 lb) of new muscle, which takes most lifters many months, raises resting expenditure by about 65 kcal a day.
comp-rmr-varies-between-people
People of the same size and composition still differ in resting metabolism
Fat-free mass explained 63 percent of the difference in basal metabolic rate between 150 adults. About a quarter of the difference was left unexplained.
comp-num-bmr-unexplained
Variation in basal metabolic rate not explained by body composition or age
What was left after fat-free mass (63 percent), fat mass (6 percent) and age (2 percent) in 150 adults.
26 % of variance
comp-big-bodies-per-kg
Larger bodies burn fewer calories per kilo at rest
The high-cost organs do not grow in step with body weight, so most extra kilos are muscle or fat and add little to resting expenditure.
comp-delayed-leanness
People often look leaner in the week after a long diet ends
For several days after calories come back up, weight and skinfolds can keep falling. Lyle McDonald named and described the effect; no study has tested it.
comp-weight-trend-feedback
A seven-day weight trend turns daily weighing into useful feedback
Students who weighed every morning and were sent the trend of their last seven readings gained no weight over a semester. Controls gained 2 to 3 kg.
comp-term-aas
Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS)

Testosterone and synthetic drugs derived from it. They build muscle (anabolic) and produce male sex characteristics (androgenic). They are prescription medicines with medical uses, carry health risks and are banned in drug-tested sport.
comp-term-supraphysiological
Supraphysiological dose
A dose that lifts a hormone above the range the body makes naturally. Testosterone trials use the term for doses several times those given to treat men with low testosterone.
comp-testosterone-without-training
In a controlled trial, testosterone built muscle and strength in men who did not train
Men given high-dose testosterone for 10 weeks with no exercise gained muscle size and strength. Men given a placebo with no exercise did not.
comp-testosterone-dose-response
Lean mass gain rose with testosterone dose in a 20-week trial
With natural production suppressed and five graded doses given, fat-free mass rose by 3.4, 5.2 and 7.9 kg (7.5, 11.5 and 17.4 lb) at the three highest doses.
comp-num-testosterone-ffm
Fat-free mass gained in 20 weeks at the highest testosterone dose tested
In healthy young men on the highest of five doses, with energy and protein intake standardized. HDL cholesterol fell as dose rose.
comp-table-testosterone-trials
What controlled testosterone trials found
Controlled trials from one research group. Doses are left out on purpose. None of this is guidance for use.
comp-mistake-enhanced-benchmark
Measuring yourself against drug-assisted physiques and programmes
Anabolic drugs add muscle that training alone does not, so the size, rate of progress and training loads of enhanced athletes do not transfer to drug-free lifters.
wom-testosterone-gap
Adult men carry at least 15 times the testosterone of adult women
After puberty men's blood testosterone runs more than 15-fold above women's, and the two ranges do not overlap in healthy adults.
wom-num-testosterone-gap
Men's circulating testosterone relative to women's
How far adult men's blood testosterone exceeds women's at any age, from a 2018 endocrine review. The two ranges do not overlap.
over 15x women's level
wom-strength-gap-upper-body
The strength gap between the sexes is widest in the upper body
Women's upper-body strength sits further below men's than their lower-body strength, mainly because less of their muscle is carried there.
wom-num-strength-share
Women's strength as a share of men's in one lab comparison
Upper- and lower-body strength of eight women against eight men. Strength per unit of muscle area did not differ between them.
52 and 66 % (upper, lower body)
wom-muscle-force-per-area
A given amount of muscle produces the same force in women and men
Strength per unit of muscle cross-section did not differ by sex, so the gap in strength is a gap in muscle size.
wom-fibre-type-share
Women's muscle has a larger share of slow-twitch fibre area
Pooled biopsies from over 5,000 people show men with bigger fibres of every type and women with more of their muscle area as type I fibre.
wom-fuel-mix
Women burn relatively more fat and less carbohydrate in steady exercise
At the same relative effort women draw more on fat and less on carbohydrate and amino acids than men, and estrogen appears to drive it.
wom-cycle-defines-physiology
The monthly cycle, not only lower testosterone, sets female physiology apart
A man's hormones stay nearly flat from day to day. A cycling woman's estrogen and progesterone swing widely every month.
wom-relative-gains-similar
Women gain muscle at the same relative rate as men on the same programme
Across 29 studies, relative muscle growth differed by under 1 percent between the sexes. Men gained slightly more in absolute terms.
wom-num-relative-growth-gap
Gap in relative muscle growth between men and women
Difference in growth relative to starting size across 29 studies that used the same training for both sexes. The interval includes zero.
wom-upper-body-strength-response
Women's upper-body strength rose faster than men's in relative terms
In 17 studies of the same programme for both sexes, women's relative upper-body strength gains were larger. Lower-body gains were similar.
wom-older-adults-pattern
After 50, men gain more in absolute terms and women as much or more in relative terms
In 30 studies of adults over 50, men added more absolute strength and size. Relative size gains matched, and women gained more relative leg strength.
wom-term-absolute-relative
Absolute and relative gains

An absolute gain is the raw change, such as 2 kg of muscle or 20 kg on a lift. A relative gain is that change as a percentage of the starting value. Sex comparisons often flip depending on which one a study reports.
wom-mistake-fear-of-bulk
Avoiding heavy weights for fear of sudden bulk
In women-only trials strength rose a lot and muscle size moderately, and the size change builds over months, not sessions.
wom-mistake-separate-method
Treating training for women as a separate method
When both sexes followed the same programme, relative gains in size and lower-body strength matched, so the same principles apply.
wom-strength-before-size
Expect strength to climb well before visible size
In a 16-week trial women's strength rose 24 to 59 percent across four tests while thigh muscle area did not change measurably.
wom-ffmi-female-athletes
Few female college athletes exceed an FFMI of about 24
Among 372 female collegiate athletes measured by DXA, mean fat-free mass index was 18.8 and the 97.5th percentile was 23.9.
wom-num-ffmi-upper
Upper FFMI threshold in female college athletes
The 97.5th percentile among 372 female collegiate athletes measured by DXA. The group mean was 18.8.
wom-lean-mass-per-height
The proposed upper limit for women's lean mass rests on one very large athlete
A 1998 study put women's ceiling above 0.44 kg of fat-free mass per cm of height. McDonald treats that as an outlier and works from about 0.33.
wom-num-lean-per-cm
McDonald's working ceiling for women's lean mass by height
His judgment of the realistic upper figure for most women, drawn from athlete samples. A coaching estimate, not a measured limit.
0.33 kg per cm (1.84 lb/in)
wom-near-limit-years
Most women are near their muscular limit after three to four years of good training
McDonald's estimate is that three to four years of proper training brings most women close to their ceiling, after which gains become very slow.
wom-table-ffm-samples
Fat-free mass measured in groups of trained women
Published samples of trained women, oldest to newest. Methods differ, so compare the rows loosely.
wom-androgens-elite
Higher natural androgen levels are more common among elite sportswomen
Polycystic ovary syndrome is over-represented in elite sport, which is one reason elite samples overstate what most women can expect.
wom-term-energy-availability
Energy availability (EA)
Energy eaten minus the energy spent in exercise, divided by fat-free mass. It is the kcal per kg of fat-free mass left each day for every other body function, including the reproductive system.
wom-ea-not-body-fat
Low energy availability, not a body fat figure, shuts down the cycle
Athletes at the same low body fat can have normal or absent cycles. The difference lies in the energy left over after training.
wom-ea-no-threshold
The 30 kcal per kg figure marks rising risk, not a switch
Newer trials found no single energy availability below which cycles fail. Risk climbs steadily as energy availability falls.
wom-num-ea-45
Energy availability linked with normal cycles and bone
The level the 2025 Female Athlete Triad update associates with being energy replete, with ovulatory cycles and normal bone density.
about 45 kcal per kg FFM per day
wom-num-ea-odds
Change in odds of a disturbed cycle per unit of energy availability
From 35 women followed over three cycles of diet and exercise. No threshold value emerged.
9% lower per 1 kcal/kg FFM higher
wom-mistake-ea-arithmetic
Trusting a calculated energy availability to the last kcal
Each part of the sum carries error: logged intake, the energy cost of exercise and the estimate of fat-free mass.
wom-term-eumenorrhea
Eumenorrhea

Regular menstrual cycles. A research guide defines it as cycle lengths of 21 to 35 days with nine or more periods in a row over a year, and asks for hormone checks before a study calls a participant eumenorrheic.
wom-term-amenorrhea
Amenorrhea (primary and secondary)

Absence of menstrual periods. Primary: periods have not begun by about age 15. Secondary: three or more periods in a row missed by a woman who has menstruated before and is not pregnant. Both need a doctor's assessment.
wom-term-oligomenorrhea
Oligomenorrhea
Infrequent periods, defined in research as cycles longer than 35 days. Causes range from energy deficiency to polycystic ovary syndrome, so the pattern needs a doctor's assessment, not a guess.
wom-term-fha
Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea (FHA)
Loss of ovulation and periods with no identifiable disease behind it, often linked to stress, weight loss, heavy exercise or a mix of these. Doctors diagnose it only after excluding other causes.
wom-term-reds
Relative energy deficiency in sport (REDs)
The International Olympic Committee's name for the health and performance problems that follow exposure to low energy availability. It applies to women and men, and diagnosis is clinical.
wom-term-triad
Female athlete triad
Three linked components in active women: energy status, reproductive function and bone health. Each runs on a spectrum from healthy to clinical, and energy deficiency starts the chain.
wom-mistake-missed-period
Treating a missed period as a normal sign of hard training
A lost or irregular cycle is a medical sign with several possible causes, and it is linked to bone loss when energy deficiency is behind it.
wom-refuel-recovery
A modest rise in intake restored periods in a year-long trial
In 76 exercising women with absent or infrequent periods, eating about 330 kcal more a day made the return of menses about twice as likely.
wom-num-refuel
Extra intake that restored menses in the REFUEL trial
Average increase achieved over 12 months by exercising women with absent or infrequent periods. The 2025 Triad update gives 300 to 600.
330 kcal per day (about 18%)
wom-pill-bleed
A bleed on the pill is not a period and says nothing about energy status
The monthly bleed on combined oral contraception is a withdrawal bleed, so it cannot show that the natural cycle is intact.
wom-hormonal-status
Hormonal status differs between women, and a study should say who it tested
Natural cycles, hormonal contraception, cycle disturbances, raised androgens and menopause are different hormonal states.
wom-term-follicular-phase
Follicular phase

The first half of the menstrual cycle, from the first day of bleeding to ovulation. Estrogen and progesterone are both low at the start. Estrogen then climbs to its peak just before ovulation while progesterone stays low.
wom-term-luteal-phase
Luteal phase

The part of the cycle that runs from ovulation to the next bleed. Progesterone reaches its highest level and estrogen stays fairly high, then both fall before the period. Body temperature runs slightly higher in this phase.
wom-table-cycle-phases
What studies found in each part of the cycle
Average findings in women with regular natural cycles. Individual women can differ from every row.
wom-cycle-performance
Cycle phase changes performance by a trivial amount on average
Pooled across 51 studies, performance in the early follicular phase was lower by a trivial margin, and the evidence was rated low quality.
wom-mistake-cycle-syncing
Rebuilding a training plan around cycle phases
Reviews of the evidence do not support fixed phase-based training rules. They recommend adjusting to the individual.
wom-checklist-cycle-log
What to log for two or three cycles before changing your plan
A short daily record shows whether your own appetite, weight and training follow the cycle, which study averages cannot tell you.
wom-luteal-intake
Women eat more in the luteal phase, by about 170 kcal a day on average
A meta-analysis of 15 datasets found energy intake about 168 kcal a day higher in the luteal phase than in the follicular phase.
wom-num-luteal-intake
Extra energy intake in the luteal phase
Average difference from the follicular phase across 15 datasets and 330 women of healthy weight. Study methods were inconsistent.
168 kcal per day
wom-mistake-luteal-metabolism
Counting on a faster metabolism before a period to cover extra eating
Resting metabolism rises only slightly in the luteal phase, and in studies since 2000 the rise was not statistically significant.
wom-cycle-tailored-diet
A diet tailored to the cycle did not beat plain restriction in its one trial
In 60 overweight women over six months, a cycle-tailored programme showed no significant advantage in the main analysis. Half the women dropped out.
wom-ocp-performance
Oral contraceptives make little or no difference to performance or training gains
Pooled data show at most a trivial average performance difference against women with natural cycles, and no effect on strength or muscle gain.
wom-contraception-weight
Trials found no large effect of hormonal contraception on body weight
Cochrane reviews found no evidence of a large weight effect from combined methods, and under 2 kg average gain in most studies of progestin-only methods.
wom-mistake-training-stops-periods
Blaming hard training itself for a lost cycle
When energy intake kept pace with exercise, hard training did not disrupt reproductive hormone pulses. Under-fuelling did.
wom-pelvic-floor
Leaking urine under heavy lifts is common in women lifters and worth getting assessed
In a survey of 480 competitive women powerlifters, 44 percent had leaked urine in the previous three months, most often on the deadlift.
wom-research-gap
About a third of participants in sport science studies are women
Across 5,261 papers from 2014 to 2020, 34 percent of participants were female, and 6 percent of studies were women-only against 31 percent men-only.
wom-num-female-participants
Female share of participants in sport and exercise science
From 5,261 papers in six journals, 2014 to 2020. Six percent of the studies enrolled only women and 31 percent only men.
34% of participants
wom-why-thin
Why the research base on women is thin
Organised sport admitted women late, and the menstrual cycle makes a well-controlled study slower and more expensive to run.
wom-table-reading-by-sample
How far a study's result carries, by who was in it
A quick way to weigh a training or diet study for a woman, from who took part and what was recorded about them.
wom-percent-vs-absolute
A diet rule given as a percentage can fail a smaller person
Women did not load muscle glycogen on a 75 percent carbohydrate diet until total energy was raised too, because their absolute intake was too low.
wom-small-calorie-budget
A smaller body leaves less room in the diet for extras
Smaller women burn less energy, so tactics sized for a large man can take up most of a day's calories.
wom-diet-trials-mostly-women
Weight-loss trials are the exception: most participants are women
In 244 lifestyle weight-loss trials, samples averaged 73 percent women, and 32 percent of trials enrolled women only.
wom-mistake-old-warnings
Treating old warnings about women and lifting as medical findings
Claims that sport masculinises women or harms fertility began as untested assertion. The sex-specific problems found since have other causes.
wom-atoz-result
In the A TO Z trial the lowest-carb diet lost most, and every group lost little
Among 311 premenopausal women, 12-month loss averaged 4.7 kg on Atkins and 1.6 to 2.6 kg on the three other diets.
wom-table-atoz
A TO Z trial: weight change at 12 months by assigned diet
Mean change in 311 overweight premenopausal women, with 95 percent confidence intervals. Only Atkins against Zone differed significantly.
wom-mistake-atoz-metabolic-advantage
Reading the A TO Z result as proof that low-carb burns more fat
Intake was self-reported, adherence drifted and the gap was small, so the trial cannot show a metabolic advantage.
wom-atoz-pattern
Most of the loss came in the first two months, while the weekly classes ran
McDonald's reading of the A TO Z weight curves: three groups lost during the class period and then stalled for ten months.
wom-atoz-adherence
Within each A TO Z diet, the women who stuck closest lost the most
The most adherent third lost 3.7 to 8.3 kg over the year, against 0.4 to 1.9 kg in the least adherent third, whatever the diet.
wom-num-atoz-adherent
Weight lost by the most and least adherent women on Atkins
Most against least adherent thirds in the A TO Z trial. The same direction held on Zone (3.7 vs 0.4) and Ornish (6.5 vs 1.7).
8.3 vs 1.9 kg in 12 months
wom-insulin-resistance-diet-choice
Insulin resistance as a guide to diet choice has mixed support
In 81 women the insulin resistant adhered and lost less on a low-fat diet, but a larger trial found no interaction between insulin secretion and diet.
wom-term-thermogenic
Thermogenic

A compound or product that raises the body's energy expenditure, often felt as warmth. Most are stimulants. McDonald puts the effect at 5 to 10 percent of energy expenditure at most, which matters little without a diet.
wom-fat-loss-supplements-small
No fat-loss supplement is required, and the proven ones add little
The few compounds with real evidence shift energy expenditure or weight by small amounts, and only alongside a diet.
wom-green-tea-women
Green tea extract did not reduce body fat in trials in women
Two placebo-controlled trials in women found no effect on weight or fat, and a high-dose trial saw liver function abnormalities in about 5 percent.
wom-caffeine-clearance
Caffeine lasts longer in the body on oral contraceptives
Women on low-dose oral contraceptives cleared caffeine more slowly, with a half-life near 7.9 hours against 5.4 in non-users.
wom-num-caffeine-half-life
Caffeine half-life with and without oral contraceptives
Elimination half-life after a single 162 mg dose in long-term users of low-dose pills against 9 matched non-users.
7.9 vs 5.4 hours
wom-caffeine-pms
Caffeine intake was not linked to developing premenstrual syndrome
In a large cohort, women with the highest caffeine intake were no more likely to develop PMS than those with the lowest.
wom-ephedrine-trials
Ephedrine produced modest extra weight loss in trials, with clear side effects
A meta-analysis found about 0.9 kg a month more loss than placebo for up to six months, and two to three and a half times the odds of adverse symptoms.
wom-yohimbine
Yohimbine has one small trial in women behind it and a known anxiety risk
Twenty obese women on 1,000 kcal a day lost 3.6 kg with yohimbine against 2.2 kg with placebo over three weeks. The trial was short and tiny.
wom-mistake-more-stimulant
Taking more of a stimulant product than the label says to speed fat loss
The serious harms linked to stimulant fat burners came with overdosing or combining them, and extra dose adds risk without adding much loss.
wom-table-fat-loss-ingredients
Fat-loss supplement ingredients: what controlled research found
Pooled or trial results for the ingredients McDonald discusses. None is needed. Ask a pharmacist or doctor about interactions before using any.
wom-term-melatonin
Melatonin

A hormone released by the pineal gland in the brain at night. It helps set the timing of sleep, and light reaching the eyes in the evening suppresses it. It also interacts with the hormones that run the reproductive cycle.
wom-melatonin-body-composition
A year of melatonin trimmed fat mass slightly in one trial of postmenopausal women
In 81 postmenopausal women, nightly melatonin for a year lowered fat mass by 6.9 percent against placebo. Body weight did not change.
wom-melatonin-bone
Melatonin raised bone density a little in two trials of postmenopausal women
A year of nightly melatonin raised femoral neck bone density by 1.4 percent against placebo, more at 3 mg than at 1 mg.
wom-table-melatonin-trials
Melatonin trials in women at a glance
Controlled evidence in three groups of women, with doses as the studies report them. Not a recommendation. Ask a doctor or pharmacist first.
wom-mistake-melatonin-proven
Treating melatonin as a proven aid for PCOS or premenstrual symptoms
Pooled trials in polycystic ovary syndrome found no effect on hormones or metabolic markers, and no trial has tested it for premenstrual symptoms.
wom-melatonin-menopause-sleep
In menopausal women melatonin helped sleep mainly where sleep was already poor
A systematic review of 24 studies found better sleep quality in postmenopausal women with existing sleep problems, and symptom relief at 3 mg or more.
wom-iron-deficiency
Iron deficiency is common in female athletes and is found by a blood test
A systematic review reports that up to 60 percent of female athletes experience iron deficiency, which lowered endurance performance by 3 to 4 percent.
hlth-who-weekly-targets
WHO asks adults for 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity a week
Aim for 150 to 300 minutes of moderate or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous aerobic activity a week, plus strength work on 2 or more days.
hlth-more-than-minimum
Mortality benefit levelled off at about two to five times the minimum
In large cohorts, the lowest death rates sat near 2 to 5 times the guideline minimum, with no clear harm at higher amounts.
hlth-steps-and-mortality
Death risk in cohorts fell with daily steps and flattened around 5,000 to 8,000
Cohort data show the steepest gains in the first thousands of steps, with 7,000 steps linked to about half the risk of 2,000.
hlth-sitting-and-activity
About an hour of daily moderate activity matched the extra risk from long sitting
People who sat over 8 hours but did about 60 to 75 minutes of moderate activity a day showed no raised mortality risk.
hlth-talk-test
The talk test finds moderate effort without a lab
If you can talk but not sing, you are in the moderate range, and if you can only say a few words, you are at vigorous effort.
hlth-zone2-definition
Zone 2 means effort just below the first lactate or ventilatory threshold
Experts define zone 2 as easy aerobic work just under the first threshold, where breathing rises but speech stays comfortable.
hlth-zone2-evidence
Evidence does not show zone 2 is the best intensity for health
A 2025 review found no proof that zone 2 is optimal and argued harder work matters for health, especially at low weekly volumes.
hlth-intervals-vo2
Interval training raised VO2 max slightly more than steady training in short trials
Pooled trials show interval training lifts VO2 max a little more than continuous training, by roughly 1 to 3 mL/kg/min.
hlth-fitness-mortality
Higher aerobic fitness goes with lower mortality, with no upper limit seen
Across large cohorts, each 1 MET higher fitness was linked to 11% to 17% lower all-cause mortality, and the top fitness group did best.
hlth-grip-mortality
Weaker grip strength tracks with higher risk of death in large cohorts
Each 5 kg (11 lb) lower grip strength went with about 16% to 20% higher all-cause mortality risk, a marker and not a proven cause.
hlth-strength-dose
About 30 to 60 minutes a week of strength training was linked to the lowest mortality
Pooled cohorts link any strength training to 10% to 17% lower mortality, with the best result near 30 to 60 minutes a week.
hlth-strength-older-adults
Resistance training builds strength, muscle and function in older adults
Progressive resistance training reliably improves strength and daily function in people aged 60 and over, and harder training works better.
hlth-muscle-loss-age
Strength falls two to five times faster than muscle size in later life
At about age 75, strength drops about 2.5% to 4% a year while muscle mass drops under 1% a year.
hlth-start-late
Raising activity in midlife was linked to similar mortality benefit to lifelong activity
Adults who stepped up activity between ages 40 and 61 had a mortality risk similar to those who were always active.
hlth-balance-falls
Exercise that challenges balance cuts falls by about a quarter in older adults at home
Falls fall about 23% with exercise in community-dwelling older adults, and balance-challenging programs of over 3 hours a week did best.
hlth-liftmor-trial
LIFTMOR: supervised heavy lifting and impact work raised spine bone density
In 101 postmenopausal women with low bone mass, eight months of supervised heavy lifting and impact work improved spine bone density.
hlth-sleep-7-hours
Adults are advised to sleep 7 or more hours a night
The AASM and SRS consensus is 7 or more hours a night for adults, and the National Sleep Foundation gives 7 to 9 for most adults.
hlth-exercise-sleep
Regular exercise gave small to moderate gains in sleep quality
Across 66 studies, regular exercise improved total sleep time and efficiency a little and sleep quality moderately.
hlth-protein-older-adults
Older adults are advised at least 1.0 to 1.2 g of protein per kg a day
Expert groups advise at least 1.0 to 1.2 g per kg (0.45 to 0.54 g per lb) a day over age 65, and more with exercise or illness.
hlth-creatine-older
Creatine plus resistance training added lean mass and some strength in older adults
Across 22 trials in adults averaging 57 to 70 years, creatine added 1.37 kg (3.0 lb) of lean mass and small strength gains.
hlth-vitamin-d
Vitamin D pills did not prevent fractures, falls or major disease in trials
Large trials and meta-analyses of vitamin D supplements found no effect on fractures, falls or major disease in general adult groups.
hlth-omega-3
Omega-3 had little effect on death or heart events but lowered triglycerides
A Cochrane review of 86 trials found little or no effect on mortality or cardiovascular events, with about a 15% drop in triglycerides.
hlth-glucose-hba1c
Fasting glucose and HbA1c have published ranges for prediabetes and diabetes
The American Diabetes Association lists prediabetes at fasting glucose 100 to 125 mg/dL or HbA1c 5.7% to 6.4%.
hlth-waist-to-height
Waist-to-height ratio of 0.5 or more marks increased health risk in NICE guidance
NICE says a waist-to-height ratio of 0.5 to 0.59 means increased health risk and 0.6 or more means further increased risk.
hlth-resting-hr
A higher resting heart rate was linked to higher mortality risk in a meta-analysis
Each 10 beats a minute higher resting rate went with 9% higher all-cause mortality risk, and readings over 80 with 45% higher.
hlth-apob
ApoB counts the particles that carry cholesterol and can disagree with LDL cholesterol
A National Lipid Association consensus says that when apoB and LDL-C disagree, risk tends to follow apoB.
hlth-mistake-age-formula
Using an age formula as your zone 2 heart rate
Age formulas give a population average, so use them as a rough guide and check against how the effort feels.
hlth-mistake-ten-thousand
Treating 10,000 steps as a pass mark
In cohorts, benefit rose steeply to about 7,000 steps, and 10,000 is a fine target without being a threshold.
hlth-mistake-predictor-target
Treating a mortality predictor as a score to chase
Grip strength and fitness predict risk in cohorts, and that does not show that pushing the number up lowers risk by a set amount.
hlth-mistake-cardio-only
Doing only walking or cardio and skipping strength and balance work
WHO advises strength work on 2 or more days for all adults and balance plus strength on 3 or more days for older adults.
hlth-n-aerobic-minutes
Weekly aerobic target for adults
WHO 2020 range for adults, or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous activity, or an equivalent mix.
150-300 min moderate per week
hlth-n-strength-days
Weekly strength days for adults
Muscle-strengthening on 2 or more days a week in WHO and US guidelines, working all major muscle groups.
2+ days per week
hlth-n-older-multicomponent
Multicomponent days for older adults
WHO advises older adults do varied activity stressing balance and strength on 3 or more days a week.
3+ days per week
hlth-n-steps-7000
Daily steps linked to about half the death risk of 2,000
In a 2025 meta-analysis, 7,000 steps a day went with 47% lower all-cause mortality than 2,000 steps.
7,000 steps per day
hlth-n-strength-minutes
Strength training time with the lowest risk
Cohort meta-analyses linked about 30 to 60 minutes a week to the largest mortality reduction.
30-60 min per week
hlth-n-sleep-hours
Sleep advised for adults
The AASM and SRS consensus recommends adults sleep 7 or more hours a night on a regular basis.
7+ hours per night
hlth-n-protein-older
Minimum protein for healthy older adults
Expert groups advise at least this much for people over 65, which is 0.45 to 0.54 g per lb.
1.0-1.2 g per kg per day
hlth-n-whtr
Waist-to-height ratio where NICE flags risk
NICE says 0.5 to 0.59 is increased health risk and 0.6 or more is further increased risk.
0.5 ratio (waist / height)
hlth-n-bp-normal
Blood pressure under which readings are normal
The AHA and ACC list under 120 systolic and under 80 diastolic as normal. Discuss readings with a clinician.
hlth-n-fasting-glucose
Fasting glucose range for prediabetes
The ADA range for impaired fasting glucose. 126 mg/dL or more is the diabetes threshold, with confirmation.
hlth-n-hba1c
HbA1c range for prediabetes
The ADA range for prediabetes by HbA1c. 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) or higher is the diabetes threshold.
hlth-n-fitness-met
Lower all-cause mortality per 1 MET fitness gain
An umbrella review linked each 1 MET higher fitness to this reduction in cohort studies.
11-17 % lower risk
hlth-t-vo2max
VO2 max
The highest rate at which your body can use oxygen during hard exercise, in mL of oxygen per kg of body weight per minute. It is the standard lab measure of aerobic fitness.
hlth-t-met
MET (metabolic equivalent)
A unit of effort. 1 MET is resting energy use, and brisk walking is about 3 to 5 METs. Fitness is often reported as the peak METs reached on a treadmill test.
hlth-t-zone2
Zone 2
Easy aerobic effort just below the first lactate or ventilatory threshold. You breathe harder but can still speak in sentences. Zone numbers vary between systems.
hlth-t-lactate-threshold
Lactate threshold
The effort above which lactate starts to build up in the blood faster than it clears. The first threshold marks the end of easy effort and varies between people.
hlth-t-sarcopenia
Sarcopenia
A condition of low muscle strength with low muscle quantity or quality, found mostly in older adults. A clinician diagnoses it using strength tests and a body measure.
hlth-t-dynapenia
Dynapenia
The age-related loss of muscle strength. In later life it runs faster than the loss of muscle size, so strength and mass are tracked separately.
hlth-t-hba1c
HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin)
A blood test that shows average blood sugar over about the past 2 to 3 months. It is given as a percentage, and published ranges separate normal, prediabetes and diabetes.
hlth-t-apob
ApoB (apolipoprotein B)
A protein carried on each cholesterol-bearing particle that can clog arteries. The blood level reflects the number of these particles and can differ from LDL cholesterol.
hlth-t-whtr
Waist-to-height ratio
Waist circumference divided by height, both in the same units. A ratio of 0.5 means the waist is half your height.
hlth-t-hazard-ratio
Hazard ratio (HR)
A figure comparing risk between groups over time. 1.0 means no difference, 0.80 means 20% lower risk and 1.20 means 20% higher. It shows association, not cause.
hlth-tbl-weekly-targets
Weekly activity targets by guideline
What WHO 2020, the US 2018 guidelines and the UK 2019 guidelines ask of adults each week.
hlth-tbl-bp-categories
Blood pressure categories (AHA and ACC)
Adult blood pressure categories in mm Hg from the AHA and ACC guideline. A clinician makes the diagnosis, and results are for discussion with a clinician.
hlth-tbl-hr-zones
A simple heart-rate zone guide
A five-zone effort guide with how each feels. Zones are a coaching convention and the boundaries differ between people and systems.
claim-train-to-failure
Do you have to train to failure to grow muscle?
Getting close to failure helps muscle growth, but reaching failure itself showed no clear extra benefit over stopping a little short.
Overstated
claim-effective-reps
Do only the last five reps of a set count?
Research on closeness to failure shows a gradual trend, not a cut-off at five reps.
Overstated
claim-light-vs-heavy
Do light weights build as much muscle as heavy ones?
For muscle size, yes when sets are hard; heavier loads still build more one-rep-max strength.

claim-twice-a-week
Does every muscle need training twice a week?
For size, weekly sets matter more than how they are split; for strength, training more often may help, though findings differ.

Is muscle soreness a sign of a good workout?
Soreness is a poor guide to muscle damage, and muscle growth does not need it.

Does cardio kill your muscle gains?
Adding cardio did not reduce overall muscle growth in a 43-study review, though a small effect showed at fibre level, mainly with running.

claim-change-exercises
Do you need to change your exercises often to keep growing?
Two small trials gave mixed results: varied exercises may help strength a little, and muscle growth was similar with or without variety.
Depends
claim-deload-fourth-week
Do you need a deload every fourth week?
Deloads are common coaching practice, but outcome trials are few; one found reduced-volume weeks did not cost muscle gain in beginners.
Depends

Is a calculated one-rep max as good as a tested one?
A set of about 5 reps predicted a max well on two exercises; accuracy fell as reps rose, and the tested lifts were not squat or deadlift.

claim-belts-weaken-core
Do lifting belts weaken your core?
No cited study shows a lifting belt weakening the core; short trials found little change in muscle activity and more reps with a belt.
Overstated
claim-need-to-max-out
Do you need to max out in training to get stronger?
Strength gains were similar across a wide range of effort, so regular true maxes are not required, though practising heavy lifts matters.
Overstated
claim-deep-squat-knees
Are deep squats bad for your knees?
One literature review found no good evidence that deep squats harm healthy knees and backs when technique is sound and load is built up gradually.
Overstated
claim-powerlifting-dangerous
Is powerlifting dangerous?
Injury rates in powerlifting were similar to other non-contact strength sports and low compared with contact sports, though the studies are weak.
Overstated
claim-periodisation-needed
Do you need a periodised program to get stronger?
Planned variation in volume and intensity gave a moderate edge for maximal strength in meta-analyses, and no clear edge for muscle size.

claim-sumo-allowed
Is a sumo deadlift allowed in competition?
Under the IPF rules the deadlift sets no stance, so sumo and conventional are both legal.
Holds up
claim-singlet-first-meet
Do you need a singlet at your first meet?
Under IPF rules, yes: a non-supportive singlet from the approved list is required in Classic (raw) competition.
Holds up
claim-belt-rules
Can you wear any lifting belt you like at an IPF meet?
No: the belt must come from the approved list and meet size and construction limits, including a maximum width of 10 cm (3.9 in).

claim-change-attempts
Can you change an attempt after you hand it in?
It depends on the attempt: the first can be changed once, second attempts cannot be changed, and the third deadlift can be changed twice.

claim-water-cut-first-meet
Is a water cut a good idea for a first meet?
Dehydration cut strength in a meta-analysis, and an IPF weigh-in about two hours before lifting leaves little time to recover, so a first meet is a poor place to try one.
Not supported
claim-sleep-before-meet
Will one bad night's sleep before a meet ruin your lifts?
One short night often has little effect on strength, but sleep restricted over several nights, and afternoon sessions after a bad night, showed bigger drops.
Depends
claim-protein-timing
Do you have to eat protein within an hour of training?
No beneficial effect of a specific protein timing showed up on lean mass or strength, so total daily protein matters more.
Overstated
claim-protein-meal-cap
Can your body only use 30 grams of protein per meal?
In one tracer study, 100 g of protein gave a bigger and longer muscle response than 25 g, so a fixed per-meal cap is not supported.
Not supported
claim-protein-kidneys
Does a high-protein diet harm healthy kidneys?
In 28 trials of adults without kidney disease, higher protein did not change the drop or rise in kidney filtration rate compared with lower protein.
Not supported
claim-bigger-surplus
Does a bigger calorie surplus build more muscle?
In one small trial, eating much more mostly added body fat, not muscle, and the best surplus size is still unknown.
Overstated
claim-creatine-kidneys
Is creatine bad for your kidneys?
In studies of healthy people, creatine did not damage the kidneys at the amounts and durations tested.
Not supported
claim-creatine-hair-loss
Does creatine cause hair loss?
The worry comes from one small study showing higher DHT; a 12-week trial that measured hair found no difference from placebo.
Overstated
claim-supplements-needed
Do you need supplements to make progress?
The IOC says supplements make a minor contribution and that only a few have good evidence of benefit.
Not supported
claim-caffeine-strength
Does caffeine help you lift more?
Caffeine gave a small boost to strength and power in a meta-analysis, clearer for upper-body strength than lower-body.
Mostly holds
claim-calculator-exact
Can a calorie calculator tell you exactly how much to eat?
No. Even the best equation misses by more than 10 percent for a share of people, so treat it as a starting point.
Not supported
claim-protein-amount
How much protein do you need to build muscle?
About 1.6 g per kg a day covers most lifters, returns shrink above that, and needs may be higher while dieting.
Mostly holds
claim-alcohol-gains
Will drinking alcohol ruin your gains?
A very heavy dose after training blunted muscle repair in one small study, and light drinking has not been tested.
Depends
claim-plant-vs-animal
Can plant protein build as much muscle as animal protein?
When total protein is enough, strength gains match, and soy matched milk protein for muscle in pooled trials. Some other plant proteins fell behind.
Mostly holds
claim-low-carb-fat-loss
Is low-carb better than low-fat for fat loss?
Trials and pooled analyses found similar weight loss on low-carb and low-fat diets, with differences too small to matter.
Not supported
claim-fasting-burns-more
Does intermittent fasting burn more fat than ordinary dieting?
With calories matched, trials of time-restricted eating mostly found no significant extra weight loss, though one meta-analysis found a small edge.
Overstated
claim-six-small-meals
Do six small meals a day speed up your metabolism?
Eating more often did not raise energy expenditure, and fewer meals did not hurt; meal count mainly affects hunger.

claim-fasted-cardio
Is fasted cardio better for fat loss?
Fasted exercise burns slightly more fat during the session, but body-mass and body-fat changes were similar in the small review that tracked them.
Overstated
claim-diet-breaks
Do diet breaks speed up fat loss?
Results are mixed: one trial found more fat loss with breaks, two syntheses found no difference in fat lost, with less hunger or less metabolic slowing.

claim-tracking-metabolism
If you track everything and cannot lose weight, is your metabolism broken?
In one careful study, people who said they could not lose weight had normal energy expenditure and were eating more than they reported.
Overstated
claim-starvation-mode
Does starvation mode stop weight loss?
Energy expenditure does fall during a diet, at rest and in non-resting activity. That slows weight loss, but no study here shows it stopping loss.
Overstated
claim-spot-reduction
Does spot reduction work?
Training one body part did not reduce fat there in most studies, though one small trial of overweight men found otherwise.

claim-one-best-diet
Is there one best diet for weight loss?
Pooled trials found modest weight loss on most diets, with minimal differences between them and effects fading by 12 months.

claim-eating-late
Does eating late at night make you gain fat?
Two small crossover trials found late eating changed hunger or energy use, but on matched calories weight loss did not differ in the trial that measured it.
Overstated
claim-out-train-bad-diet
Can you out-train a bad diet?
In pooled trials, exercise alone produced modest weight loss, so it is a weak tool for offsetting a poor diet.
Overstated
claim-loss-rate-muscle
Can you lose weight fast without losing muscle?
Slower is safer for muscle: about 0.5 to 1 percent of body weight a week. With hard lifting, lean mass also held in short trials of faster loss or a steep deficit.

claim-dieting-hunger
Do you just have to put up with hunger when you diet?
Some hunger comes with a deficit, but protein, water-rich whole foods and enough sleep each lowered it in trials.
Overstated
claim-scale-stalled
Has your diet stopped working if the scale has not moved in two weeks?
Probably not. Two-week weight changes are mostly water, so judge a weekly average over three to four weeks of honest logging.
Overstated
claim-set-point
Does your body have a set point it fights to defend?
Your body does push back when you lose weight, but a single fixed set point does not explain why body weight has risen across populations.
Overstated
claim-regain-after-diet
Does everyone regain the weight after a diet?
Most people regain a lot, but not all of it, and a minority keep most of it off by staying active and weighing themselves.
Overstated
claim-recomposition
Can you build muscle and lose fat at the same time?
Yes for beginners and people with more fat to lose. It is likely slow or marginal for lean, advanced lifters.

claim-sleep-fat-loss
Does sleep matter for fat loss if your calories are right?
In one small trial on the same diet, short sleep cut the share of weight lost as fat by 55% and raised the loss of fat-free mass.

claim-zone-2-best
Is Zone 2 the best cardio intensity for health?
Higher fitness is linked to lower risk of death, but that is about being fit, and a 2025 review found evidence does not support Zone 2 as the best intensity.
Overstated
claim-10000-steps
Do you need 10,000 steps a day?
Risk of death fell steeply up to roughly 5,000 to 7,000 steps in a large review, with 10,000 not a threshold; these are observational data.
Overstated
claim-lifting-early-death
Does lifting weights lower the risk of early death?
People who lifted had lower mortality in cohort studies, with the biggest drop at roughly 30 to 60 minutes a week; this shows association, not proof.

claim-lifting-stunts-growth
Does lifting weights stunt growth in teenagers?
A review of 22 youth training programs found no effect on height or weight growth in pre- and early-pubertal youth, with supervised programs relatively safe.

claim-bmi-useless-lifters
Is BMI useless for lifters?
BMI misclassifies some muscular athletes, but it is a rough screen that also misses excess fat in many other people.
Overstated
claim-nuts-weight-gain
Do nuts make you put on weight?
In trials, adding nuts did not raise body weight, and people who ate more nuts were slightly less likely to become overweight.
Not supported
claim-diet-drinks-weight
Do diet drinks with artificial sweeteners make you gain weight?
Swapping sugary drinks for diet drinks led to slightly lower weight in trials; against water, the lower-certainty comparison showed no clear weight difference.
Not supported
claim-watch-calories
Can a fitness watch tell you how many calories you burned?
Wrist devices track heart rate fairly well, but in a lab test of seven wrist devices, none estimated calories within 20%.
Overstated
claim-exercise-with-cold
Is it safe to work out when you have a cold?
In young adults, moderate exercise during a mild head cold did not make it worse or longer in a controlled trial. Fever and chest symptoms were not tested.
Depends
claim-cramps-dehydration
Are muscle cramps during exercise caused by dehydration or low salt?
In a large race, cramping went with faster pacing and a history of cramps, not with fluid loss or blood salt levels.
Overstated
claim-keto-build-muscle
Can you build muscle on a ketogenic diet?
People doing resistance training on ketogenic diets lost more fat and more fat-free mass; in trained lifters without planned restriction, no clear difference.
Depends
claim-morning-lifting
Do you gain less muscle and strength if you lift in the morning?
Morning and evening training built similar strength and muscle, though strength is on average higher in the evening at the start.
Not supported
claim-cold-room-fat-loss
Does keeping your home cold help you burn off fat?
Mild cold raises energy use by a few percent, but studies of people who got used to the cold found little change in body weight.
Overstated
claim-missed-meal-metabolism
Does skipping meals or fasting for a day slow your metabolism?
Resting energy use did not fall after a day of very low intake, and it rose over the first three days of a total fast.
Not supported
claim-eat-fat-burn-fat
Is eating extra fat the way to burn body fat?
Cutting carbohydrate raises the fat you burn, yet on equal calories cutting fat removed more body fat in a ward study.
Not supported
claim-zero-calorie-label
Is a food labelled zero calories truly calorie-free?
US labels may show 0 calories for anything under 5 a serving and 0 g fat for under 0.5 g, so large or repeated servings still add energy.
Not supported
claim-run-zones-on-bike
Can you use your running heart rate zones on the bike?
Heart rate at threshold on a treadmill did not predict heart rate at threshold on a bike, so each sport needs its own test.
Not supported
claim-water-best-rehydration
Is plain water the best drink after a sweaty session?
In men, restoring fluid after heavy sweating took more drink than was lost, with enough sodium. At rest, milk and rehydration solutions were retained longer than water.
Depends
claim-train-other-limb
Does training one arm protect the other while it is immobilized?
Training the free limb reduced strength loss in a limb held still, with a smaller effect on muscle size, in healthy volunteers.
Depends
